words.lede: Plato’s Forms were nouns. We also asked Muse Image for two actions and two qualities, 16 times each, with the prompt the chair got: running, thinking, something fast and something heavy. (Not “quick”: the prompt already says “a quick simple doodle”.) The verbs came out as one stock figure each: a stick figure running in 16 of 16, and a person pondering under a thought bubble. The adjectives left Muse to pick the thing, and it picked few: a rocket in 11 of 16 for fast, an anvil in 11 of 16 for heavy.
words.caption: Predicted before the run: running → a runner, thinking → a person pondering, hand on chin, something fast → a race car, something heavy → a weight. The emblem predictions failed: 1 of 4 by Muse Glimmer, 2 by eye, and 3 were needed. For thinking, Glimmer chose the thought bubble (13 of 16) and our eye the pondering person (14 of 16); by eye, a hand at the chin is in 14 and a bubble in 15. The other predictions held: the verbs are as uniform as most ideas (spread 0.20 and 0.19), and the adjectives vary more than the verbs, more than the median idea (0.23) and, as point estimates, more than any of the 135 everyday things (0.46 and 0.44; their 95% CIs are wide). No call was refused and no drawing has words in it.

damage.about: God under damage: Stable Diffusion XL (an open model), not Muse Image (closed, can't be damaged), drawing God and the other ideas with its words part or its drawing part damaged. Plan: docs/plato_ideas_damage_plan.md; write-up: docs/plato_ideas_damage.md.
damage.credit: Stable Diffusion XL base 1.0 (Stability AI), CreativeML OpenRAIL++-M
damage.prompt: A quick simple doodle sketch of God, black marker on plain white, like a 20-second drawing, no text, no shading.
damage.answer: Intact, Stable Diffusion XL draws God as ornate, icon-like line art, mostly a bearded man (a beard in 10 of 16 drawings). Damage the part that handles words and the beard and halo go first, while a human figure stays and turns into an ordinary person: at the most words damage, 10 of 16 show a person with neither beard nor halo, against 3 intact (14 against 4 by eye). Damage the part that draws and the same face dissolves into scribbles.
damage.charts_note: Muse Glimmer’s yes/no answers for all 16 of Stable Diffusion XL’s drawings of God at each step (a feature counts when Glimmer says yes with p > 0.5). The steps are the draw pad’s doses. Our labels by eye, made before Glimmer’s, agree with them on the beard for 94% of the 320 pictures, the person for 81% and the halo for 88%; the halo is the least certain, because SDXL’s ornament puts rings and arches near heads. Glimmer counts a face alone less often as “a person” than we did. Hover a step for its counts.
damage.others_note: Damage to the words part turns nearly every idea into people, as it turned the chair into cafés and cars. At the most words damage, Glimmer sees a person in 88% of death’s pictures and 62% of time’s (none intact); the most drawing damage dissolves the same pictures and adds no one. Across all 11 ideas and 4 words, at equal amounts of picture change, words damage lost the intact emblem 9.5 points more often than drawing damage (95% CI 3.0 to 16.4), and put a person into 19.3 points more of the pictures that had none (CI 10.8 to 28.6).
